sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Cornus sericea, red osier dogwood, is a deciduous North American shrub 1.8–2.7 m tall and wide, common along banks, wetlands and marsh edges. Its young twigs are bright red.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: White flowers appear in summer and develop into white, often bluish-tinged drupes eaten by birds. The plate matches the red stems and pale fruits. It differs from Eurasian Cornus sanguinea, which has black fruits.
